title: 04. OOP: Metaclasses
summary: In Python, everything is an object — including classes themselves. A Metaclass is the class of a class.

sections.title: EXPLANATION

diagrams.title: Classes are created by metaclasses
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  src["class Model(Base): ..."] --> body["execute the class body into a namespace dict"]
  body --> meta["metaclass(name, bases, namespace) — type by default"]
  meta --> cls["class object Model"]
  cls --> inst["Model() — instances"]
  hook["__init_subclass__ — lighter hook for most needs"] -.-> cls
diagrams.explain: Just as objects are instances of classes, classes are instances of **metaclasses** (`type` by default). A custom metaclass can register, validate or rewrite classes as they are defined — ORMs use this — but `__init_subclass__` or a class decorator covers most use cases more simply.
